fields.reasoning: The leaf's statement says ship check 'never says a failure is unrelated to the plan' and its acceptance asserts no detail contains 'unrelated'; Decision plan-ci-flake-reruns chose a .rhiza-only fact over a cause claim because a check that reads .rhiza/ (Rhiza's own self-check) can fail on a plan's content, and Decision plan-ci-flake-source-summary-matches already corrected the Source to that design. Only the handle still names the rejected design, so a builder reading it, or plan-run-reruns-ci-flakes's dependency by handle, is pointed the wrong way. rhiza apply's set op takes a new handle on the same node, so the rename keeps the ID and every link; the dependency follows the node. The critic's suggested name describes exactly what the leaf adds: the rerun count and the .rhiza-only note. Changing the statement to match the handle instead would reintroduce the possibly false claim.
fields.statement: Rename leaf 01M6WJ6ZEEPYS69MVFGK79HHKN from ship-check-names-unrelated-failure to ship-check-failure-names-reruns-and-rhiza-only-diff (a set with a new handle on the same node, so its ID, fields, decided-by link to plan-ci-flake-reruns and plan-run-reruns-ci-flakes's depends-on link are kept). The leaf's statement and acceptance stay unchanged; any text that names the old handle is updated to the new one.
